name: Lab 1
tasks: Configure SW-1 switch port E0/1 to carry traffic for the Cisco IP phone and PC
Configure SW-2 E0/1 to carry traffic for PC2
Configure VLAN 10 with the name “Engineering” on SW-1
Configure the link between SW-1 and SW-2 to use the vendor neutral neighbor discovery protocol
Configure the link on SW-1 to R1 so that it does not allow the Cisco neighbor discovery protocol to pass
tasks_text:
R1 has been pre-configured with all the necessary commands. All physical cabling is in place and verified. Connectivity to the end devices must be configured.
1. Configure SW-1 switch port E0/1 to carry traffic for the Cisco IP phone and PC
2. Configure SW-2 E0/1 to carry traffic for PC2
3. Configure VLAN 10 with the name “Engineering” on SW-1
4. Configure the link between SW-1 and SW-2 to use the vendor neutral neighbor discovery protocol
5. Configure the link on SW-1 to R1 so that it does not allow the Cisco neighbor discovery protocol to pass
solution_text:
Task 1. Configure SW-1 switch port E0/1 to carry traffic for the Cisco IP phone and PC
On SW-1:
SW-1(config)#int e0/1
SW-1(config-if)#switchport mode access
SW-1(config-if)#switchport access vlan 10
SW-1(config-if)#switchport voice vlan 11
Task 2. Configure SW-2 E0/1 to carry traffic for PC2
On SW-2
SW-2(config)#int e0/1
SW-2(config-if)#switchport mode access
SW-2(config-if)#switchport access vlan 30
Task 3. Configure VLAN 10 with the name “Engineering” on SW-1
On SW-1
SW-1(config)#vlan 10
SW-1(config-vlan)#name Engineering
SW-1(config-vlan)#exit //to apply the config
Task 4. Configure the link between SW-1 and SW-2 to use the vendor neutral neighbor discovery protocol
“vendor neutral neighbor discovery protocol” means LLDP. LLDP must be enabled on the device before you can enable or disable it on any interfaces.
On both SW-1 and SW-2:
SW-1,SW-2(config)#lldp run
SW-1,SW-2(config)#int e0/0
SW-1,SW-2(config-if)#lldp transmit
SW-1,SW-2(config-if)#lldp receive
Task 5. Configure the link on SW-1 to R1 so that it does not allow the Cisco neighbor discovery protocol to pass
SW-1(config)#int e0/2
SW-1(config-if)#no cdp enable
Save the configuration
SW-1#, SW-2#copy running-config startup-config

tasks_text:

1. Configure Sw1 and Sw2 with both VLANS, naming them according to the VLAN Name provided in the topology.
2. Configure the E0/1, E0/2, and E0/3 ports on both switches for both VLANS and ensure that Cisco IP phones and PCs pass traffic.
3. Configure Sw1 and Sw2 to allow neighbor discovery via the vendor-neutral protocol on e0/0.
solution_text:
Task 1. Configure Sw1 and Sw2 with both VLANS, naming them according to the VLAN Name provided in the topology.
On both switches:
Sw1,Sw2(config)#vlan 77
Sw1,Sw2(config-vlan)#name User_VLAN

Task 2. Configure the E0/1, E0/2, and E0/3 ports on both switches for both VLANS and ensure that Cisco IP phones and PCs pass traffic.
On both switches:

Sw1,Sw2(config-if)#switchport mode access
Sw1,Sw2(config-if)#switchport access vlan 77
Sw1,Sw2(config-if)#switchport voice vlan 177
Task 3. Configure Sw1 and Sw2 to allow neighbor discovery via the vendor-neutral protocol on e0/0.
On both switches:

--output omitted--

name: Lab 3
tasks: All relevant ports are pre-configured as
Configure SW-1 port E0/0 to permit only VLANS 5 and 6
Configure both SW-1 and SW-2’s E0/1 ports to send and receive untagged traffic over VLAN 77
Configure SW-2 E0/2 port to permit only VLAN 6

Configure both SW-3 and SW-4 ports e0/0 and e0/1 for link aggregation using the industry standard protocol with the following requirements:
+ SW-3 ports must immediately negotiate the aggregation protocol
+ SW-4 ports must not initiate the negotiation for the aggregation protocol
+ Use the designated number assignment
tasks_text:
All physical cabling is in place and verified. Router R1 is configured and passing traffic for VLANs 5 and 6. All relevant ports are pre-configured as 802.1q trunks.
1. Configure SW-1 port E0/0 to permit only VLANS 5 and 6
2. Configure both SW-1 and SW-2’s E0/1 ports to send and receive untagged traffic over VLAN 77
3. Configure SW-2 E0/2 port to permit only VLAN 6
4. Configure both SW-3 and SW-4 ports e0/0 and e0/1 for link aggregation using the industry standard protocol with the following requirements:
+ SW-3 ports must immediately negotiate the aggregation protocol
+ SW-4 ports must not initiate the negotiation for the aggregation protocol
+ Use the designated number assignment
solution_text:
Task 1. Configure SW-1 port E0/0 to permit only VLANS 5 and 6
SW-1(config)#int e0/0
SW-1(config-if)#switchport trunk allowed vlan 5,6
Task 2. Configure both SW-1 and SW-2’s E0/1 ports to send and receive untagged traffic over VLAN 77
Only traffic from native VLAN are sent untagged so we need to configure VLAN 77 the native VLAN.
On both SW-1 and SW-2:
SW-1#,SW-2(config)#int e0/1
SW-1#,SW-2(config-if)#switchport trunk native vlan 77
Task 3. Configure SW-2 E0/2 port to permit only VLAN 6
SW-2(config)#int e0/2
SW-2(config-if)#switchport trunk allowed vlan 6
Task 4. Configure both SW-3 and SW-4 ports e0/0 and e0/1 for link aggregation using the industry standard protocol with the following requirements:
+ SW-3 ports must immediately negotiate the aggregation protocol
+ SW-4 ports must not initiate the negotiation for the aggregation protocol
+ Use the designated number assignment
The link aggregation using the industry standard protocol is LACP. From the exhibit, we learned that the “designated number assignment” is Po34. On SW-3 we must use mode “active” while on SW-4 we must use mode “passive”.
On SW-3:
SW-3(config)#int range e0/0 - 1
SW-3(config-if-range)#channel-group 34 mode active
On SW-4:
SW-4(config)#int range e0/0 - 1
SW-4(config-if-range)#channel-group 34 mode passive
Note: We don’t need to configure trunking Po34 interface.
Save the configuration
SW-1#, SW-2#, SW3#, SW-4#copy running-config startup-config

name: Lab 4
tasks: Configure static routing that ensures traffic sourced from R1 will take an alternate path through R3 to PC1 in the event of an outage along the primary path
Configure default routes on R1 and R3 to the Internet using the least number of hops
tasks_text:
All physical cabling is in place. Router R4 and PC1 are fully configured and inaccessible. R4’s WAN interfaces use .4 in the last octet for each subnet. Configurations should ensure that connectivity is established end-to-end.
1 . Configure static routing to ensure R1 prefers the path through R2 to reach only PC1 on R4’s LAN
2. Configure static routing that ensures traffic sourced from R1 will take an alternate path through R3 to PC1 in the event of an outage along the primary path
3. Configure default routes on R1 and R3 to the Internet using the least number of hops
solution_text:
First we should use the “show ip interface brief” on R2 & R3. Suppose the IP addresses of
+ interface E0/0 on R2 is 10.0.12.2
+ interface E0/0 on R3 is 10.0.13.3
Task 1. Configure static routing to ensure R1 prefers the path through R2 to reach only PC1 on R4’s LAN
R1(config)#ip route 10.0.41.10 255.255.255.255 10.0.12.2
Task 2. Configure static routing that ensures traffic sourced from R1 will take an alternate path through R3 to PC1 in the event of an outage along the primary path
We can configure a floating static route with highest Administrator Distance (254) as a backup route:
R1(config)#ip route 10.0.41.10 255.255.255.255 10.0.13.3 254
Task 3. Configure default routes on R1 and R3 to the Internet using the least number of hops
On R1:
R1(config)#ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 10.0.13.3
On R3:
R3(config)#ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 209.165.201.1
Save the configuration
R1#, R3#copy running-config startup-config

2. For the IPv4 /28 subnet, router R1 must be configured with the first usable host address.
3. For the IPv4 /28 subnet, router R2 must be configured with the last usable host address.
4. For the IPv6 /64 subnet, configure the routers with the IP addressing provided from the topology.
5. A ping must work between the routers on the IPv4 and IPv6 address ranges.
solution_text:
Task 1 + Task 2 + Task 3
The network 192.168.180.0/28 is unavailable so the next subnet is 192.168.180.16/28 (increment: 16). This subnet ranges from 192.168.180.16 to 192.168.180.31.
Therefore the first usable host address is 192.168.180.17/28 and the last usable host address is 192.168.180.30/28. We will them for two E0/1 interfaces:
R1(config)#interface e0/1
R1(config-if)#ip address 192.168.180.17 255.255.255.240
R1(config-if)#no shut
R2(config)#interface e0/1

R2(config-if)#no shut
Task 4. For the IPv6 /64 subnet, configure the routers with the IP addressing provided from the topology.
Note: IPv6 routing has been configured so we don’t need to do it.
On R1:
R1(config)#interface e0/1
R1(config-if)#ipv6 address 2001:db8:acca::1/64
On R2:
R2(config)#interface e0/1
R2(config-if)#ipv6 address 2001:db8:acca::2/64
Task 5. A ping must work between the routers on the IPv4 and IPv6 address ranges.
R1#ping 192.168.180.30
.!!!!
R1#ping ipv6 2001:db8:acca::2
!!!!!
Save the configuration
R1,R2#copy running-config startup-config

SW-2#(config)#interface e0/2

name: Lab 7
tasks_text: Reference
solution_text:
Task 1:
+ Configure R1 with the first usable host IP address in the IPv4 network.
+ Configure R2 with the last usable host IP address in the IPv4 network.
In the subnet 10.0.12.4/30 (increment: 4), the network address is 10.0.12.4 & the broadcast address is 10.0.12.7. Therefore the first usable host IP address is 10.0.12.5 while the last usable host IP address is 10.0.12.6.
On R1:
R1(config)#interface e0/0
R1(config-if)#ip address 10.0.12.5 255.255.255.252
R1(config-if)#no shut
On R2:
R2(config)#interface e0/0
R2(config-if)#ip address 10.0.12.6 255.255.255.252
R2(config-if)#no shut
+ Verify connectivity using ping.
On R1:
R1(config-if)#exit
R1(config)#exit
R1#ping 10.0.12.6
.!!!! -> ping successful
Task 2:
+ Do not assign the subnet router anycast address to either router.
+ Configure R1 with the first usable host IP address in the IPv6 network.
+ Configure R2 with the last usable host IP address in the IPv6 network.
Note: The subnet router anycast address is the lowest address in the subnet, so it looks like the “network address”. For example, if the prefix for the subnet is 2001:db8:12::/126 then the subnet router anycast address for that subnet is 2001:db8:12::.
Since we are working with 2001:db8:12::/126 then the first 126 binary bits are the prefix and we have 2128-126 = 22 = 4 host addresses in this subnet. 2001:db8:12::0 is the network address (or subnet router anycast address) while other 3 host addresses are in range from 2001:db8:12::1 to 2001:db8:12::3.
Since IPv6 does not reserve the last address as a broadcast address, 2001:db8:12::3 is the last usable host address. The first usable host address is 2001:db8:12::1.
On R1:
R1(config)#interface e0/0
R1(config-if)#ipv6 address 2001:db8:12::1/126
On R2:
R2(config)#interface e0/0
R2(config-if)#ipv6 address 2001:db8:12::3/126
+ Verify connectivity using ping.
R1#ping 2001:db8:12::3
!!!!! -> successful
Save the configuration
R1#, R2#copy running-config startup-config

name: Lab 9
tasks: Configure OSPF Area 0 with Process ID 110 on all devices under their respective interfaces connected to VLAN

To accomplish this, do not use the network command under the OSPF process.
Task

Configure R1 to always be the DR and Sw101 always to be the BDR.
R2 and R3 should be configured not to participate in the DR/BDR election.
tasks_text:
Task 1. Configure OSPF Area 0 with Process ID 110 on all devices under their respective interfaces connected to VLAN101.
To accomplish this, do not use the network command under the OSPF process.
Task 2. Configure R1 to always be the DR and Sw101 always to be the BDR.
R2 and R3 should be configured not to participate in the DR/BDR election.
solution_text:
Task 1. Configure OSPF Area 0 with Process ID 110 on all devices under their respective interfaces connected to VLAN101. To accomplish this, do not use the network command under the OSPF process.
On R1:
R1(config)#interface e0/2
R1(config-if)#ip ospf 110 area 0
On R2:
R2(config)#interface e0/1
R2(config-if)#ip ospf 110 area 0
On R3:
R3(config)#interface e0/0
R3(config-if)#ip ospf 110 area 0
On Sw101:
Sw101(config)#interface vlan101
Sw101(config-if)#ip ospf 110 area 0
Verification
SW101#sh ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID     Pri   State           Dead Time   Address         Interface
10.3.3.3          1   FULL/BDR        00:00:36    10.101.101.3    Vlan101
10.1.1.1          1   FULL/DROTHER    00:00:30    10.101.101.1    Vlan101
10.2.2.2          1   FULL/DROTHER    00:00:32    10.101.101.2    Vlan101
Task 2. Configure R1 to always be the DR and Sw101 always to be the BDR. R2 and R3 should be configured not to participate in the DR/BDR election.
On R1, we need to set the OSPF priority of 255 (highest) so that R1 is always the DR. On Sw101, we set the OSPF priority of 254 or any lower value which is different from 0 so that Sw101 is always the BDR.
On R1 (Suppose we are still under interface E0/2):
R1(config-if)#ip ospf priority 255
On Sw101 (Suppose we are still under interface Vlan101):
Sw101(config-if)#ip ospf priority 254
R2 & R3 do not participate in DR/BDR election so we set their OSPF priority to 0:
On R2 (Suppose we are still under interface E0/1):
R2(config-if)#ip ospf priority 0
On R3 (Suppose we are still under interface E0/0):
R3(config-if)#ip ospf priority 0
We should clear the OSPF process on Sw101 to see the result:
On Sw101
Sw101(config-if)#exit
Sw101(config)#exit
Sw101#clear ip ospf process
Reset ALL OSPF processes? [no]: y
Note: We can use the “do clear ip ospf process” command instead using two “exit” commands above.
Verification
R1#show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID     Pri   State           Dead Time   Address         Interface
10.2.2.2          0   FULL/DROTHER    00:00:36    10.101.101.2    Vlan101
10.3.3.3          0   FULL/DROTHER    00:00:30    10.101.101.3    Vlan101
10.1.1.1        255   FULL/DR         00:00:35    10.101.101.1    Vlan101
-> R1 (10.1.1.1) is now the DR. R2 (10.2.2.2) & R3 (10.3.3.3) are DOTHERs so we can deduce Sw101 is BDR.
Save the configuration
R1#, R2#, R3#, Sw101#copy running-config startup-config

tasks_text:
Refer to the topology. All physical cabling is in place. Routers 2 and 3 are inaccessible. Configure OSPF routing for the network and ensure R1 has joined Area 0 without using network statements.
Task 1. Configure OSPF on R1 with a process ID and router- ID only as follows:

Task 2
– Configure R1 to establish neighbor adjacencies with R2 and R3. The network statement under the OSPF process must not be used.

solution_text:
Task 1. Configure OSPF on R1 with a process ID and router- ID only as follows:
– use process ID 33
– use E0/1 IP as the router ID
First use the “show ip interface brief” command on R1 to get the E0/1 IP address:
R1#show ip interface brief
Interface              IP-Address      OK? Method Status                Protocol
Ethernet0/0            10.0.22.1       YES Manual     up                      up
Ethernet0/1            10.0.33.1       YES Manual     up                      up
-> The IP address of E0/1 is 10.0.33.1 so we will use it to configure the OSPF router ID.
Note: Please check the IP address of E0/1 interface carefully as the IP address may be different.
On R1:
R1(config)#router ospf 33
R1(config-router)#router-id 10.0.33.1
Task 2
– Configure R1 to establish neighbor adjacencies with R2 and R3. The network statement under the OSPF process must not be used.
– Configure R1 to always become the DR for Area 0
On R1:
R1(config-router)#exit
R1(config)#interface e0/0
R1(config-if)#ip ospf 33 area 0
R1(config-if)#ip ospf priority 255
R1(config-if)#interface e0/1
R1(config-if)#ip ospf 33 area 0
R1(config-if)#ip ospf priority 255
Verification
We should clear the current OSPF process to make sure DR is elected again.
R1(config-if)#exit
R1(config)#exit
R1#clear ip ospf process
Reset ALL OSPF processes? [no]: y
Then verify with the “show ip ospf neighbor” or “show ip ospf interface” command:
R1#show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID     Pri   State           Dead Time   Address         Interface
10.2.2.2          1   FULL/BDR        00:00:35    10.0.22.2       GigabitEthernet0/0
10.3.3.3          1   FULL/BDR        00:00:35    10.0.33.3       GigabitEthernet0/1
or
R1#show ip ospf interface
Ethernet0/0 is up, line protocol is up
Internet address is 10.0.22.1/30, Area 0
Process ID 33, Router ID 10.0.33.1, Network Type BROADCAST, Cost: 1
Transmit Delay is 1 sec, State DR, Priority 255
...
Ethernet0/1 is up, line protocol is up
Internet address is 10.0.33.1/29, Area 0
Process ID 33, Router ID 10.0.33.1, Network Type BROADCAST, Cost: 1
Transmit Delay is 1 sec, State DR, Priority 255
-> Interfaces E0/0 & E0/1 of R1 are DRs.

name: Lab 15
tasks_text:
Configure IPv4 and IPv6 between two routers.
Task 1:
+ Configure R1 with the first usable host IP address in the in4 network.
+ Configure R2 with the last usable host IP address in the IPv4 network.
+ Verify connectivity using ping.
Task 2:
+ Do not assign the subnet router anycast address to either router.
+ Configure R1 with the first usable host IP address in the IPv6 network.
+ Configure R2 with the last usable host IP address in the IPv6 network.
+ Verify connectivity using ping.
solution_text:
Task 1. Configure R1 with the first usable host IP address in the in4 network. Configure R2 with the last usable host IP address in the IPv4 network. Verify connectivity using ping.
In the subnet 192.168.168.192/28 (increment: 16), the network address is 192.168.168.192 & the broadcast address is 192.168.168.207. Therefore the first usable host IP address is 192.168.168.193 while the last usable host IP address is 192.168.168.206.
On R1:
R1(config)#interface e0/1
R1(config-if)#ip address 192.168.168.193 255.255.255.240
R1(config-if)#no shut
On R2:
R2(config)#interface e0/1
R2(config-if)#ip address 192.168.168.206 255.255.255.240
R2(config-if)#no shut
+ Verify connectivity using ping.
On R1:
R1(config-if)#exit
R1(config)#exit
R1#ping 192.168.168.206
.!!!! -> ping successful
Task 2. Do not assign the subnet router anycast address to either router. Configure R1 with the first usable host IP address in the IPv6 network. Configure R2 with the last usable host IP address in the IPv6 network. Verify connectivity using ping.
Note: The subnet router anycast address is the lowest address in the subnet, so it looks like the “network address”. For example, if the prefix for the subnet is 2001:db8:12::60/125 then the subnet router anycast address for that subnet is 2001:db8:12::60.
Since we are working with 2001:db8:12::60/125 then the first 125 binary bits are the prefix and we have 2128-125 = 23 = 8 host addresses in this subnet. 2001:db8:12::60 is the network address (or subnet router anycast address) while other 7 host addresses are in range from 2001:db8:12::61 to 2001:db8:12::67.
Since IPv6 does not reserve the last address as a broadcast address, 2001:db8:12::67 is the last usable host address. The first usable host address is 2001:db8:12::61.
On R1:
R1(config)#interface e0/1
R1(config-if)#ipv6 address 2001:db8:12::61/125
On R2:
R2(config)#interface e0/1
R2(config-if)#ipv6 address 2001:db8:12::67/125
+ Verify connectivity using ping.
R1#ping 2001:db8:12::67
!!!!! -> successful
Save the configuration
R1#, R2#copy running-config startup-config

solution_text:
Task 1. Configure SW-2 and SW-3 ports E0/0 to use the industry standard encapsulation method for trunking and only tag VLAN 10
+ “use the industry standard encapsulation method for trunking” -> use 802.1Q
+ “only tag VLAN 10” -> only allow VLAN 10

Task 3. Configure SW-2 and SW-3 ports E0/2 and E0/3 to use the industry standard encapsulation method for trunking and tag all VLANs

SW-2,SW-3(config-if)#switchport mode trunk

+ “SW-3 ports must immediately negotiate” -> SW-3 uses active mode

On SW-2:
SW-2(config)#interface range e0/2 - 3
SW-2(config-if)#channel-group 23 mode passive
On SW-3:
SW-3(config)#interface range e0/2 - 3
SW-3(config-if)#channel-group 23 mode active

Only when Port-channel 23 goes up, all the configs under E0/2 & E0/3 will be copied to this port-channel interface automatically

tasks_text:
Refer to the topology. All physical cabling is in place. Routers HQ2 and HQ3 are inaccessible. Configure OSPF routing for the network and ensure HQ1 has joined Area 0 as the Designated Router (DR).
Task 1. Configure OSPF on HQ1 and ensure HQ2 and HQ3 become neighbors.
+ use process ID 111
+ use Lo0 IP as the router ID
+ advertise connected networks using an inverted subnet mask to match the exact prefixes used
Task 2. Ensure HQ1 always becomes the DR for Area 0 on all links.
solution_text:
Task 1. Configure OSPF on HQ1 and ensure HQ2 and HQ3 become neighbors. (use process ID 111; use Lo0 IP as the router ID; advertise connected networks using an inverted subnet mask to match the exact prefixes used)
On HQ1, use “show run” command to find out the IP addresses along with subnet masks of all interfaces:
HQ1#show run
...
interface Loopback0
ip address 10.110.110.110 255.255.255.255
!
interface Ethernet0/0
ip address 10.0.112.1 255.255.255.252
!
interface Etherenet0/1
ip address 10.0.113.1 255.255.255.248
!
We will use the IP address of Loopback0 interface to configure OSPF router ID as requested.
On HQ1:
HQ1(config)#router ospf 111
HQ1(config-router)#router-id 10.110.110.110
Advertise connected networks using an inverted subnet mask to match the exact prefixes used:
HQ1(config-router)#network 10.110.110.110 0.0.0.0 area 0
HQ1(config-router)#network 10.0.112.0 0.0.0.3 area 0
HQ1(config-router)#network 10.0.113.0 0.0.0.7 area 0
Note: To advertise Loopback0 with 0.0.0.0 wildcard mask, we have to use the IP address of Lo0 interface itself (10.110.110.110), not its network (10.110.110.0).
Verification
HQ1#show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID          Pri   State           Dead Time   Address         Interface
10.130.130.130         1   FULL/DR         00:00:37    10.10.113.3     Ethernet0/1
10.120.120.120         1   FULL/DR         00:00:37    10.10.112.2     Ethernet0/0
Task 2. Ensure HQ1 always becomes the DR for Area 0 on all links.
To make sure HQ1 always becomes the DR we need to set the OSPF priority to maximum value of 255 on all physical interfaces:
HQ1(config)#interface range e0/0 - 1
HQ1(config-if-range)#ip ospf priority 255
Verification
We should reset the OSPF process first with “clear ip ospf process” command to make sure HQ1 becomes the DR:
HQ1#clear ip ospf process
Reset ALL OSPF processes? [no]: y
HQ1#show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID         Pri   State           Dead Time   Address         Interface
10.130.130.130        1   FULL/BDR        00:00:37    10.10.113.3     Ethernet0/1
10.120.120.120        1   FULL/BDR        00:00:37    10.10.112.2     Ethernet0/0
-> HQ2 & HQ3 became BDRs so surely HQ1 became DR.
or we can use the “show ip ospf interface” to see all physical interfaces of HQ1 became DRs directly.
Save the configuration
HQ1#copy running-config startup-config

solution_text:
Task 1. Using the minimum number of ACEs, configure an extended named ACL and place it within the topology to conserve as many resources as possible. ACL requirements are: + ACL name = WWW_ACL; + Allow HTTP traffic only from VLAN 202; + Block telnet only for PC1; + Allow all other traffic
– If we put the ACL on Sw3, we may need to put it at two interface VLANs. Also it may not control all types of traffic.
– If we put the ACL on Sw1, we also need to place it on two interfaces e0/2 & e0/0 (in case e0/2 fails)
-> The ACL should be placed on R1.
On R1:
R1(config)#ip access-list extended WWW_ACL
R1(config-ext-nacl)#permit tcp 10.101.1.0 0.0.0.255 any eq www
R1(config-ext-nacl)#deny tcp any any eq www
R1(config-ext-nacl)#deny tcp host 10.101.0.2 any eq telnet
R1(config-ext-nacl)#permit ip any any
R1(config-ext-nacl)#exit
R1(config)#interface e0/1
R1(config-if)#ip access-group WWW_ACL in
Note: For the request “Allow HTTP traffic only from VLAN 202”, we need two statements: “permit tcp 10.101.1.0 0.0.0.255 any eq www” and “deny tcp any any eq www”.
Verification
Try to telnet to R1 from PC1:
On PC1:
C:\>telnet 10.1.0.2
Trying 10.1.0.2 ...
% Connection timed out; remote host not responding
Check the access-list on R1 to see the telnet was filtered out:
R1#sh ip access-lists
Extended IP access list WWW_ACL
10 permit tcp 10.101.1.0 0.0.0.255 any eq www
20 deny tcp host 10.101.0.2 any eq telnet (12 match(es))
30 permit ip any any (25 match(es))
Task 2. Configure a local account on Sw2 with telnet access only on virtual ports 0-4. Use the following information: + Username: AdminGroup; + Password: BumBL3d; + Algorithm type: Scrypt; + Privilege level: Exec mode
On Sw2:
Sw2(config)#username AdminGroup privilege 15 algorithm-type scrypt secret BumBL3d
Sw2(config)#line vty 0 4
Sw2(config-line)#transport input telnet
Sw2(config-line)#login local
Note: Privilege level 15 is known as “enable mode” or “privileged exec mode,” and authorizes all commands by default. We cannot use the keyword “password” after “algorithm-type scrypt” so we need to use the keyword “secret” instead.
Task 3. Configure Sw3: + Enable DHCP Snooping for VLANs 102 and 202; + Enable DHCP Snooping MAC address verification
On Sw3:
Sw3(config)#ip dhcp snooping //Enable DHCP Snooping feature
Sw3(config)#ip dhcp snooping vlan 102,202 //Enable DHCP Snooping for VLAN 102,202 only
Sw3(config)#ip dhcp snooping verify mac-address //Globally enables MAC address verification for DHCP snooping on all switch interfaces.
Save the configuration
R1#,Sw2#,Sw101#copy running-config startup-config
